turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start, but I have a client call at 4:40. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
You need an answer? I asked you a question first, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

I'm writing that down: Owen "admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM" or it goes on his transcript. My son doesn't admit to something he didn't do, and your own procedure says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment with nothing on his record. You can explain that threat to the principal today, or you can tell me what you actually have besides a machine's guess.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

"The only two options." Neither of them is in your school's procedure, Hale, and I'm not picking either. Show me what you have, or I'm walking down to the principal's office the moment we're done here.
